quotes.text: When celebrities or influencers endorse investment opportunities, including crypto asset securities, it doesn't mean that those investment products are right for all investors.

Celebrity endorsements of cryptocurrency create measurable short-term price spikes exploited as exit windows by promoters, with retail investors of lower financial literacy significantly more susceptible regardless of age or income.

how_to.name: How to verify whether a celebrity actually endorses a crypto project
how_to.description: Four-step protocol to confirm the legitimacy of any celebrity crypto promotion before taking financial action.

steps.name: Cross-reference official channels
steps.text: Visit the celebrity verified website and authenticated social media profiles. Look for platform-native verification badges, not badge images pasted into profile pictures. If the endorsement does not appear on these channels, it is almost certainly fabricated.

steps.name: Reverse search the media
steps.text: For video, upload clips to InVID WeVerify or use Google reverse video search. For images, run a Google Reverse Image Search or TinEye lookup. For text, search the exact quoted phrase in quotation marks.

steps.name: Check regulatory databases
steps.text: Search the SEC EDGAR database for any registered offering tied to the promoted project. Check the FTC scam alert page at consumer.ftc.gov. In the UK, search the FCA Warning List for unauthorized firms.

steps.name: Report
steps.text: Report to ReportFraud.ftc.gov and FBI IC3 (ic3.gov) in the US, Action Fraud (actionfraud.police.uk) in the UK, and the hosting platform impersonation report form.
